questions.name: Equilateral Triangles: construct a triangle of side 4 cm
questions.s_figure: An equilateral triangle ABC with AB = BC = CA = 4 cm, built on the base AB with an arc of radius 4 cm from A and an arc of radius 4 cm from B crossing at C.

questions.name: Triangles from Three Sides: construct 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm
questions.s_figure: Triangle ABC with the base AB = 4 cm, AC = 5 cm and BC = 6 cm, with the arc of radius 5 cm from A and the arc of radius 6 cm from B crossing at C.

The five triangles built from the given lengths, each drawn with its sides labelled: (a) 4, 4, 6, (b) 3, 4, 5, (c) 1, 5, 5, (d) 4, 6, 8 and (e) 3.5, 3.5, 3.5 centimetres, with the equal sides marked on (a), (c) and (e).

questions.q_figure: A circle with its centre marked by a dot and no other points marked.
questions.s_figure: The circle with centre O and two points P and Q on it, with OP, OQ and PQ drawn and OP and OQ marked equal, giving the isosceles triangle OPQ.

questions.q_figure: Two circles of the same size overlapping so that each passes through the centre of the other, with centres A and B marked, and beside them three circles of the same size with centres A, B and C, each passing through the centres of the other two.
questions.s_figure: The two circles with their crossing points C and D marked and the triangles ABC and ABD drawn between the centres and the crossing points, then the three circles with the triangle ABC drawn between the centres.

questions.name: Triangle Inequality: try 3, 4, 8 and 2, 3, 6
questions.s_figure: A base AB of 8 cm with an arc of 3 cm from A and an arc of 4 cm from B that stop short of each other, and below it a base of 6 cm with an arc of 2 cm from one end and an arc of 3 cm from the other that do not meet.

questions.name: Triangle Inequality: do 10, 15 and 30 make a triangle
questions.s_figure: A rough triangle ABC with AB = 15 cm, BC = 10 cm and CA = 30 cm marked on its sides.

questions.name: Triangle Inequality: lengths 3, 3 and 7
questions.s_figure: A base of 7 cm with an arc of radius 3 cm drawn from each end, the two arcs stopping short of each other with a gap between them.

questions.name: Lengths 4, 5 and 8: does a triangle exist
questions.s_figure: A base AB of 8 cm with a circle of radius 4 cm centred at A meeting AB at X and a circle of radius 5 cm centred at B, the two circles crossing at two points, with AX = 4 cm and BX = 4 cm marked.

questions.name: Two Sides and the Angle: construct 5 cm, 45° and 4 cm
questions.s_figure: Triangle ABC with AB = 5 cm along the base, an angle of 45° at A, AC = 4 cm along the arm from A, and BC joined with BC about 3.6 cm.

Three triangles built from the given sides and angle: (a) sides 3 cm and 7 cm with a 75° angle between them, (b) sides 6 cm and 3 cm with a 25° angle, (c) sides 3 cm and 8 cm with a 120° angle, each with its third side joined and labelled about 6.9 cm, 3.5 cm and 9.8 cm.

questions.name: Two Angles and the Side: construct 45°, 5 cm and 80°
questions.s_figure: Triangle ABC with AB = 5 cm, an angle of 45° at A and an angle of 80° at B, the two arms crossing at C, with AC about 6.0 cm, BC about 4.3 cm and the angle at C equal to 55°.
Three triangles built on a base with an angle at each end: (a) 75°, 5 cm, 75°, (b) 25°, 3 cm, 60° and (c) 120°, 6 cm, 30°, with the third angle marked as 30°, 95° and 30°.

questions.name: Two Angles That Fail: smallest angle at B beside 40°
questions.q_figure: A horizontal segment AB with a line l starting at A and rising to the right at an angle of 40° to AB, and the point B at the other end of the base.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with the line m drawn through B parallel to l, and the angle at B marked 140° on the same side of AB as the 40° angle at A.

questions.name: Third Angle: 60° and 70° on bases of 5 cm and 7 cm
questions.s_figure: Two triangles side by side: one on a base of 5 cm and one on a base of 7 cm, each with angles 60° and 70° at the ends of its base and the angle at the top vertex marked 50°.

questions.name: Third Angle: finding A from 50° and 70°
questions.q_figure: A triangle ABC with the vertex A at the top, the angle at B marked 50° and the angle at C marked 70°.
questions.s_figure: The same triangle with the line XY drawn through A parallel to BC, the alternate angles XAB = 50° and YAC = 70° marked, and the angle BAC = 60° between them.

questions.q_figure: A triangle ABC with the angle at A marked 50° and the angles at B and C marked as equal.

questions.name: Angle Sum: proof with a parallel line and a paper fold
questions.s_figure: A triangle ABC with the line XY drawn through A parallel to BC, the angles XAB and B marked alike, the angles YAC and C marked alike, and the angle at A between them, the three angles together along the straight line XY.

questions.name: Exterior Angles: finding ACD from 50° and 60°
questions.q_figure: A triangle ABC with the side BC extended beyond C to a point D and the exterior angle ACD marked.
questions.s_figure: The same triangle with the angles A = 50°, B = 60° and ACB = 70° marked and the exterior angle ACD = 110° shown as equal to 50° + 60°.

questions.name: Altitudes: an altitude outside an obtuse triangle
questions.q_figure: A triangle ABC with a wide obtuse angle at B, the base BC along the bottom with B on the left and C on the right, and A above and to the left of B.
questions.s_figure: The same triangle with the base BC extended to the left beyond B and a dashed perpendicular from A meeting the extension at D, the right angle at D marked.

questions.name: Altitudes: draw one with a set square
questions.s_figure: A triangle ABC with the base BC along a ruler, a set square against the ruler with its upright edge touching A, and the altitude AD drawn from A to BC with the right angle at D marked.

questions.name: Altitudes: a side that is also an altitude
questions.q_figure: A triangle ABC with the right angle at B marked, B at the bottom left, A directly above B and C to the right of B.
questions.s_figure: The same triangle with AB marked as the altitude from A to BC, BC marked as the altitude from C to AB, and the altitude from B to the long side AC drawn inside the triangle.
Triangle ABC with BC = 5 cm, AB = 6 cm and CA = 5 cm and the altitude AD drawn from A to BC with the right angle at D marked and AD about 4.8 cm.

A base AC of 5 cm with three different right-angled triangles drawn on it, each with the right angle at B, for example with the angle at A equal to 30°, 45° and 70°.
Two isosceles triangles: a right-angled one with two equal sides of 4 cm and angles 90°, 45° and 45°, and an obtuse-angled one with two equal sides of 5 cm and angles 120°, 30° and 30°.
